title: Calibration of Doubt, Inference and Certainty

sections.content:
You know *dudo que* and *quizás* from B1 Unit 13. In analytical and critical writing, choosing between indicative and subjunctive lets you calibrate how strongly you stand behind an inference or how much ambiguity remains.

Affirmative verbs of certainty, deduction and suspicion (*deducir que*, *inferir que*, *sospechar que*, *presuponer que*, *es indudable que*) declare a claim as real and take the **indicative**: *Deduzco que la respuesta es ambigua.* Once you negate that certainty or cast doubt (*no creo que*, *dudo que*, *no es seguro que*, *no está claro que*), Spanish switches to the **subjunctive**: *No está claro que la frase tenga una sola lectura.*

Watch negated *no dudar*: because *no dudo que* expresses certainty, it normally takes the **indicative** (*No dudo que el autor buscaba precisión*), whereas affirmative *dudo que* takes the **subjunctive** (*Dudo que el lector note esa ambigüedad*).

sections.title: Certainty / inference vs. doubt
rows: Sospecho que el texto es ambiguo a propósito.
No dudo que presuponen una lectura previa.
No es seguro que podamos inferir su intención.
Dudo que todos deduzcan lo mismo de esa frase.

items.spanish: Sospecho que la ambigüedad del comunicado responde a una estrategia consciente.
items.english: I suspect that the ambiguity of the statement reflects a deliberate strategy.

items.spanish: Dudo que el público infiera esa conclusión sin una explicación más clara.
items.english: I doubt that the audience will infer that conclusion without a clearer explanation.

items.spanish: No es seguro que el contrato presuponga un acuerdo previo entre las partes.
items.english: It is not certain that the contract presupposes a prior agreement between the parties.

items.spanish: De sus palabras deduzco que el mensaje era deliberadamente ambiguo.
items.english: From his words I deduce that the message was deliberately ambiguous.

sections.content: Remember the flip with *dudar*: affirmative *dudo que* triggers the subjunctive, while negative *no dudo (de) que* expresses certainty and takes the indicative. Likewise, affirmative *sospechar que* takes the indicative (*Sospecho que miente*), while *no creer que* takes the subjunctive (*No creo que mienta*).
